 Learn more US stocks fell on Thursday as Alphabet's Q3 earnings sparked a sell-off in the stock and AI jitters returned to markets, dragging on the tech-heavy indexes. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell almost 0.3%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost roughly 0.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell about 1.4%. 
 Tech stocks snapped a positive run this week as investors digested the Fed's rate pause on Wednesday and earnings from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), the parent company of Google. Microsoft beat analyst expectations on the top and bottom lines, while Alphabet's sales came up short . Cloud growth was up 103%, but concerns about the tech giant's free cash flow and AI return on investment were the albatross around the company's stock, which sank more than 12%. 
 ( ^DJI )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 52,342.56 -132.54 (-0.25%) At close: October 29 at 4:33:51 PM EDT ^DJI ^GSPC ^IXIC A sell-off in AI names spread, as the iShares Semiconductor Index ETF ( SOXX ) skidded and software stocks ( IGV ) also tumbled, with double-digit losses for Fortinet ( FTNT ) and ServiceNow ( NOW ) following their earnings reports. 
 Markets will get another dose of hyperscaler earnings after the bell on Thursday when Amazon ( AMZN ) reports results. Several other stocks were moving on individual earnings: Eli Lilly ( LLY ), for example, popped 6% following strong Q3 results for its GLP-1 drugs. Caterpillar's ( CAT ) stock fell as much as 12% after the industrial giant's forecast failed to impress Wall Street. Shares of grocery chain Sprouts ( SFM ) plunged 22% in the wake of disclosing a price-cutting strategy expected to weigh on profits into next year. 
 Thursday's market action comes after the Federal Reserve held rates unchanged on Wednesday afternoon. The decision had two dissenters who favored a rate hike amid sticky inflation. Meanwhile, a fresh reading of the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge showed prices heated up in September, with the Personal Consumption Expenditures index rising 3.6% year over year. 
 LIVE COVERAGE IS OVER 22 updates Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:18 PM UTC Ines Ferré Intel stocks sinks 17% as revenue outlook falls short of estimates amid declining PC sales
 Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports: 
 Intel ( INTC ) reported better-than-anticipated third-quarter earnings after the bell Thursday, but Q4 revenue outlook fell short of Wall Street's expectations on declining PC sales. 
 Intel stock fell more than 20% on the news before paring losses. 
 In the fourth quarter, Intel is projecting revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the $17 billion analysts expected. 
 Intel says the shortfall is a result of a worse-than-anticipated drop in PC revenue. The industry is contending with two overlapping factors at the moment: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises around the world to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand. 
 Read more here. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:15 PM UTC Ines Ferré Rivian stock pops in after hours after EV maker posts upbeat Q3 results, boosts full-year guidance
 Rivian ( RIVN ) stock jumped in after hours after the EV maker reported upbeat third quarter results after the bell on Thursday and boosted its guidance, citing strong R2 sales. 
 Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian reports: 
 Rivian reported Q3 revenue of $2.155 billion vs. $2.02 billion per Bloomberg consensus, up 38% from a year ago. Rivian posted an adjusted loss per share of $0.48 vs. $0.61, and an adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) loss of $435 million vs. $575.9 million, narrower than the $602 million loss from last year. 
 Read more here. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:12 PM UTC Ines Ferré Amazon stock sinks in after-hours following quarterly results
 Amazon ( AMZN ) stock tanked 10% in post-market hours before trimming losses following the e-commerce giant's quarterly results. 
 Amazon maintained its 2026 capex at $220 billion for its AI infrastructure buildout. 
 Meanwhile, free cash flow decreased to an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing twelve months ended September 30. That's down from an inflow of $14.8 billion for the same period a year ago. 
 Read more here. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:01 PM UTC Ines Ferré Alphabet stock sinks, software stocks weigh on tech sector 
 US stocks dropped on Thursday after Alphabet's third quarter earnings failed to impress Investors. Shares of Google's parent company dropped more than 12%. 
 Software stocks declined after outlooks from ServiceNow ( NOW ) and Fortinet ( FTNT ) further heightened AI jitters. 
 Investors rotated into defensive sectors such as Healthcare ( XLV ), Financials ( XLF ), and Real Estate ( XLRE ), keeping a lid on overall market losses. 
 Sector action on Thursday, Oct. 29 The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) dropped almost 0.3%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost roughly 0.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell nearly 1.4%. 
 Investors shifted focus to the upcoming results from e-commerce giant Amazon ( AMZN ), which reports after the close. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 7:17 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell ADT stock surges to 5-year high after Thrive Holdings agrees to $7.6 billion buyout deal
 Home security company ADT ( ADT ) agreed on Thursday to be acquired and taken private by Thrive Holdings in an all-cash deal that values the company at $7.6 billion. 
 Thrive Holdings will pay $10 per share in cash for ADT, representing a 45.6% premium over ADT stock's closing price on Oct. 27. 
 ADT stock soared 34% to around $9.93 per share on the news, putting it on pace for its highest close since August 2021. 
 Thrive Holdings is a private capital group founded by Josh Kushner and backed by OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), focused on acquiring enterprise businesses for the long term and advancing their artificial intelligence and technological capabilities. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:36 PM UTC David Hollerith The S&P 493 is beating the 'Magnificent Seven'
 Investors have been rotating out of some of the stock market's biggest and most favored giants for the last two weeks, turning the so-called Magnificent Seven into something of a drag on major indexes.  
 The Defiance Large CAP ex-MAG 7 ( XMAG ), a lesser-known exchange-traded fund that tracks 493 large-cap stocks and excludes Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ,  GOOG ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Meta ( META ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and Nvidia ( NVDA ), has in recent days pulled ahead of the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) for the year.  
 As of Thursday afternoon, XMAG is up more than 15% for the year, compared to 13% for the S&P 500 over the same period. The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF ( MAGS ) is up less than 6%. 
 The Magnificent Seven have dominated Wall Street and the stock market's attention since the beginning of the AI boom. If the group's recent run as laggards holds, Wall Street may need a new nickname for hip stocks. It might also suggest how investors are positioning themselves amid the artificial intelligence frenzy.  
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:05 PM UTC Ines Ferré These 3 sectors could be in focus next year in Washington — no matter who wins on Tuesday
 Yahoo Finance's Ben Werschkul reports: 
 The 2026 campaign has featured bipartisan calls for action on pharmaceuticals, the housing market, and AI data centers, a sign that this trio of sectors may be in focus in Washington no matter which party prevails on Tuesday. 
 The critical comments are especially notable coming from Republicans. Democratic rhetoric about reining in big business is nothing new, but the GOP's focus indicates both an increased willingness within the party to adopt a populist stance and a potential openness to strike deals in the new power-sharing landscape. 
 And the high likelihood of Democrats winning control of at least one chamber of Congress could also elevate these issues — with or without President Trump's support. 
 While Democrats are now strongly favored to win a majority in the House in next week's midterms, the Senate is less clear, and a 60-vote threshold there means action would require bipartisan buy-in within any scenario. 
 Read more here. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 5:17 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Crocs stock soars 25% as HeyDude sales return to growth
 Crocs ( CROX ) stock soared 25% on Thursday to its highest price in over two years as investors cheered on a return to growth for the footwear company's HeyDude loafer brand and a brighter outlook for 2026 sales. 
 In the third quarter, HeyDude revenue increased 6.1% over the previous year to $170 million, marking the first sales increase in six quarters for the struggling shoe brand. 
 Crocs bought HeyDude for $2.5 billion in 2022, its largest acquisition ever. But the brand struggled amid excess inventory and discounting, causing investors to become fed up with lagging sales. 
 HeyDude makes up roughly 16% of Crocs' total revenue, while the flagship Crocs brand accounts for the remaining 84% of sales. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 4:02 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Software stocks get crushed after ServiceNow, Fortinet Q3 earnings reports
 Software stocks tumbled on Thursday, led by a 25% drop in ServiceNow ( NOW ) stock and a 21% loss for Fortinet ( FTNT ). 
 The iShares software sector ETF ( IGV ) fell 4%. Other software names, including Oracle ( ORCL ), Salesforce ( CRM ), and Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ). 
 AlphaSpace heatmap Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré explains what's behind the move: 
 Fortinet's third quarter results beat estimates, but its full-year service revenue forecast was lowered to $5.15 billion to $5.17 billion, down from its previous guidance of $5.18 billion to $5.22 billion and below Wall Street estimates of $5.2 billion, according to Bloomberg data. 
 "Fortinet's cut to service revenue guidance implies lower attach rates from bundled networking and secure access service edge offerings on its firewall platform," noted Bloomberg Intelligence analysts. 
 Following the results, Wall Street analysts lowered their valuations on the stock, with BofA cutting Fortinet to Neutral and setting a price target of $140 per share. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:06 PM UTC Carvana stock jumps as on record quarter, vehicle sales
 Carvana ( CVNA ) shares surged 15% after the online car retailer reported a 42.4% year-over-year increase in third-quarter revenue to $8.04 billion, marking its first quarter with sales exceeding $8 billion. 
 Retail vehicle sales rose 39% to 217,385 units, surpassing 200,000 vehicles in a single quarter for the first time. 
 Carvana said it refinanced $1.7 billion of senior secured notes, a move expected to cut annual interest expense by about $45 million. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:17 PM UTC Ines Ferré Caterpillar stock drops as AI boom jitters resurface
 Caterpillar ( CAT ) shares plunged as much as 12% before trimming losses after the heavy equipment maker's third quarter results only modestly exceeded Wall Street expectations, with adjusted earnings of $7.20 a share and revenue of $20.68 billion. 
 The industrial giant also forecast moderate sales growth in the fourth quarter, disappointing investors who had expected stronger results from a key beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom. 
 The company's power and energy unit, which builds generators and gas turbines for AI data centers, has surged amid the AI boom as the segment's sales have surpassed the big yellow excavators and farming equipment for which it is best known. 
 Catapillar's order backlog reached a record $78 billion. However, concerns over rising data center costs, project delays, and growing political opposition to new facilities have weighed on sentiment. 
 The stock is off nearly 40% from its June peak. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:07 PM UTC David Hollerith Sprout's stock drops 18% as grocery chain embarks on price slashing strategy
 Shares of Sprout's Farmers Market ( SFM ) plunged 18% Thursday after the grocery chain cut its profit outlook and announced aggressive price cuts in a bid to win back shoppers.  
 The Phoenix, Ariz.-based specialty supermarket is embarking on a price-slashing strategy that's now expected to weigh on profits into next year as it's seeing fewer customers. 
 "We do not expect a smooth road ahead," JPMorgan analyst Thomas Palmer wrote to clients Thursday, describing the earnings reduction as "massive" but keeping its "overweight" rating on the grocery chain. 
 After warning about third quarter earnings, Sprouts told analysts on Tuesday it expects Q4 earnings of between $0.47 and $0.51 per share, well below the $1.21 analysts had anticipated, according to S&P Global data. 
 The company cited increasingly price-sensitive customers, along with this year's outbreak of the foodborne parasite cyclospora, as key headwinds driving the sales decline. It's also in the midst of a CEO transition after Sprouts announced last month that COO Nicholas Konat will take over for current CEO Jack Sinclair in early January. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 1:59 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell PCE inflation shows prices ticked higher in September, keeping expectations for a year-end hike
 Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger reports: 
 A fresh reading of the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge showed prices heated up in September, solidifying expectations for an interest rate hike in December. 
 The Personal Consumption Expenditures index rose 3.6%, in line with expectations and up from 3.4% a month earlier. On a core basis, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, PCE rose 3.1%, also in line with expectations and up a tenth of a percentage point from 3% in August. Month over month, core PCE clocked in at 0.3%, in line with projections, marking a faster pace from the 0.2% seen in August. 
 The data was anticipated, prompting many analysts to feel a rate hike was in order Wednesday, given other inflation readings ahead of the Fed's meeting that showed price increases last month. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 1:58 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell US GDP accelerates to 3.4% in the third quarter
 Yahoo Finance's Molly Moorhead reports: 
 The US economy grew at a robust pace in the third quarter, driven by investment, consumer spending, and government spending. 
 Gross domestic product increased at a 3.4% annualized rat e, according to an initial estimate released Thursday by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis, beating economists' expectations of 3.1% and marking an acceleration from the second quarter's 2.2% growth. 
 Third-quarter growth was partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are subtracted in the calculation of GDP, increased. The artificial intelligence build-out was the main engine, with business investment surging 12.7%. Consumer spending grew 3.8%, matching the rate in Q2 and the strongest since the end of 2024. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 1:53 PM UTC Jared Blikre Alphabet heads for a $500 billion drop in market value, the biggest in its history
 Alphabet ( GOOGL ) is on track for its worst day ever. The stock fell about 13% Thursday after its third quarter results , steeper than any session since it went public in 2004. 
 That puts nearly $500 billion of stock market value on the line, the second-biggest one-day loss ever for a US-listed company. Only Nvidia ( NVDA ) has lost more, about $593 billion on Jan. 27, 2025, the day China's DeepSeek rattled AI investors. 
 Alphabet would need to close at about $274.75, down roughly 15%, to take Nvidia's record, by Yahoo Finance calculations. It has already blown past the $400 billion SpaceX ( SPCX ) lost on June 22, the previous No. 2. 
 Read More: 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 1:38 PM UTC David Hollerith US stocks open lower as tech trade wobbles
 US stocks opened lower Thursday after disappointing earnings from industry giant Alphabet ( GOOGL ) dragged down indexes. 
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.6%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) lost 0.5%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell 1.4%. 
 ( ^DJI )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 52,342.56 -132.54 (-0.25%) At close: October 29 at 4:33:51 PM EDT ^DJI ^GSPC ^IXIC Alphabet stock sank after its quarterly sales disappointed , while Microsoft ( MSFT ) held up better following its report. 
 The moves come as investors continue to scrutinize whether massive spending on artificial intelligence is translating quickly enough into earnings growth across Big Tech. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:23 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma DoorDash acquires Instacart for $17 billion, doubling down on hyper-local delivery
 DoorDash ( DASH ) announced plans to acquire hyper-local grocery delivery provider Instacart ( CART ) on Thursday morning in a deal valued at $17 billion. 
 DoorDash, which is primarily known for its restaurant food delivery business, will pay $65 per Instacart share, a 26% premium over the stock's Oct. 22 closing price. The transaction includes 75% cash, with Instacart stockholders able to elect cash, DoorDash stock, or a combination of both. Instacart's board of directors unanimously approved the deal, according to a press release. 
 "Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online," DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the release. "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery." 
 DoorDash stock popped over 5% in premarket trading, while Instacart stock edged lower. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:11 PM UTC Ines Ferré Lumentum stock jumps on report of possible merger with Marvell
 Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) stock dropped 11% on Thursday on reports that the AI chipmaker is in advanced talks to purchase optical parts maker Lumentum ( LITE ). Shares of Lumentum surged 5%. 
 The potential multibillion-dollar mega deal between the semiconductor designer and Lumentum was first reported by Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter. 
 An agreement could be announced as soon as next week. Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion, compared with Marvell's roughly $221 billion. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Robinhood is seeing retail investor habits change dramatically as stock trading cools
 Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban reports: 
 Retail investors are changing the way they trade. 
 While overall retail volumes are declining , as Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider wrote in a recent note, money is shifting away from traditional equities. 
 Instead, more investors are pouring their funds into options, leveraged ETFs, and prediction markets. Robinhood's ( HOOD ) latest earnings offer a window into the shift . 
 The online brokerage reported weaker-than-expected profits earlier this week as declining interest income and rising expenses weighed on the company. But it also drew record trading activity in stocks, options, and prediction markets. 
 Robinhood said revenue from prediction markets increased more than 500% from this time last year, up to $173 million. Customers traded a record 16.4 billion contracts during the past quarter. 
 Read more. 
 Thu, October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Oil declines as traders parse signs of fresh diplomacy on Iran
 Bloomberg reports: 
 Oil dropped as traders weighed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran. 
 West Texas Intermediate fell toward $102 a barrel, after rising almost 3% in the previous session, while Brent closed near $115. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran continued to give diplomacy chance, and the Wall Street Journal reported US Vice President JD Vance had reached out to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the nation's top security body. 
 President Donald Trump told Axios on Wednesday that negotiations were taking place through mediators but stressed he didn't know whether they would bear fruit. "We need to finish the job — either through a deal or another way — we will find out if negotiations can succeed," he was quoted as saying.
